title: The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower #shorts

lines.text: Can you sell the Eiffel Tower? In nineteen twenty-five, one man did.
Victor Lustig posed as a government official and invited five scrap dealers to a fancy hotel.
He said Paris could not afford the tower, so it would be sold for scrap.
One dealer, Andre Poisson, paid up, and even bribed him to win the deal.
Lustig fled to Austria. Poisson was too embarrassed to go to the police.
So Lustig tried to sell the tower again.
So, can you sell the Eiffel Tower? In Paris, one man did, and the tower is still standing.

facts.year: 1925, after Gustave Eiffel's death (toureiffel.paris, Mental Floss)
facts.method: posed as a Parisian civil servant, wrote bogus official letters to the five most prominent scrap dealers, met them in a hotel suite
facts.victim: scrap dealer Andre Poisson paid and also paid a bribe; roughly 7,300 tons of iron
facts.aftermath: Poisson too embarrassed to press charges; Lustig fled to Austria and later tried to sell the tower again (that victim went to police)
